ops.title: daemonkit and its consumers: drop the per-connection security checks? (Oct 27 2026)
ops.body:
Owner, verbatim: "if the stupid secuty stuff is adding overhead get rid of tia ll just simplify tejh processes can jstu be tursted implicitly".
Confirmed scope (all five): (1) remove code-signature, team-ID and entitlement verification of connecting processes (internal/trust peer checks); (2) remove the separate code-signed control connection and fold it into the one connection; (3) replace SHA-256 hashing of the binary for build identity with the build's version string; (4) remove the per-command launchctl check; (5) remove the per-tool trust settings and requirements in cc-present, cc-slack, cc-review and cc-interact. Any same-user process may connect; no same-UID check is kept.
Kept: cc-present's network token for LAN/tailnet clients (iOS, other machines), and daemonkit deploy's install-time app-bundle signature verification.
Supersedes answer 939ba43 (the Ensure fast path): with no re-hash and no launchctl check per command, the fast path is moot.
